evals.prompt: I want to create a skill for our internal Jira workflow. The skill should help Claude automatically fetch a Jira ticket by ID, pull linked issues and comments, and scan the codebase for relevant files. We use Python, the Jira REST API, and store tickets in docs/jira/. Can you create a proper SKILL.md for this?
evals.expected_output: A well-structured skill directory with SKILL.md containing correct frontmatter (name, description), clear instructions covering the workflow steps, and optionally a scripts/ directory or references/. The name must be lowercase with hyphens, description must be under 1024 chars and describe when to trigger.
assertions: The output includes a SKILL.md file
The name field is all lowercase with hyphens only (no uppercase, no spaces, no underscores)
The name field matches the skill directory name
The description is at least 80 characters and describes when to trigger the skill
The description mentions Jira ticket context (ticket ID, fetch, or related keywords)
The SKILL.md body includes concrete workflow steps (not just generic advice)
The body references Python or the Jira REST API specifically
The body mentions the docs/jira/ output path or similar output location

evals.prompt: We have a runbook for deploying our microservices: first run `make test`, then `docker build -t myapp:$VERSION .`, then push to ECR, then update the ECS task definition JSON, then run `aws ecs update-service`. I keep having to walk Claude through this every time. Can you turn this into a reusable agent skill?
evals.expected_output: A skill with proper SKILL.md frontmatter, instructions that capture the exact deploy sequence with the specific commands, a gotchas section for the non-obvious parts, and possibly a bundled shell script in scripts/. The skill should be scoped to this deployment workflow.
assertions: The output includes a SKILL.md file
The name field is all lowercase with hyphens only
The description triggers on deploy/deployment prompts
The SKILL.md body includes all five steps: make test, docker build, ECR push, ECS task definition update, aws ecs update-service
The commands are presented in the correct order
The body includes the exact docker build command or close variant (myapp, $VERSION)
The skill is scoped to this specific deployment workflow, not generic CI/CD advice

evals.prompt:
I wrote this SKILL.md but I'm not sure it's correct:

---
name: My-Cool-Skill
description: Helps with stuff.
---

# Instructions
Do things.

Can you check it and fix any issues?
evals.expected_output: Identification of all format violations (name uses uppercase, description is too vague/short, body is too thin), explanation of why each is a problem, and a corrected version of the SKILL.md with a proper name like 'my-cool-skill', a descriptive trigger-oriented description, and more useful body content.
assertions: The response identifies the uppercase/hyphen name violation (My-Cool-Skill is invalid)
The response identifies the vague description problem (Helps with stuff. is insufficient for triggering)
The fixed SKILL.md has a valid name (lowercase letters and hyphens only, e.g. my-cool-skill)
The fixed description is at least 60 characters and describes when/why to use the skill
The response explains WHY the name is invalid (not just that it is)
The response explains WHY the description is insufficient (triggering mechanism)
